# Component

* [Building blocks and starting points (the simplified panel)](building-blocks-and-starting-points.md) (draft) - How the designer app is organised since 2026-10-23 (shoulder straps added 2026-10-24: tank, narrow, thin, racer, with the neckline and back running between them): a leotard is built from elements (neckline, back, sleeves, leg, front top, waist seam) picked one at a time, each change keeping the rest of the design (block.set, with a dry run that lists what a change would take away so the panel asks first); six code-defined starting points (start.apply) beside the moodboard designs; the Move tool (orbit, select, drag a point) and a five-tool rail; the piece pane with material, colour, gradient and cut-out up front; materials ordered by moodboard frequency; settings and rare controls behind the settings popover and More disclosures. Includes the reconciliation rules and pitfalls.
* [Garment cutting from curves (arrangement)](garment-cutting.md) - How app/src/garment/ turns the document's curves into panels: projected surface splines, attached end points, insertion of every polyline into the canonical mesh, per-face planar subdivision, pruning, sliver merging, cells and panel seeds, with the tolerances and failure fallbacks that make it robust.
* [Garment sliding over the posed body (experiment)](garment-sliding.md) (draft) - Why a leotard painted on the skin's vertices goes wrong in deep poses (leg openings dragged down the inner thigh, seams warped at the armpit), and the experimental fix in app/src/body/slide.js: the garment slides over the posed body under tension, as-rigid-as-possible against its A-pose shape, with measured results on the low lunge and kneeling poses.
* [Pattern pieces and flattening](pattern-pieces-and-flattening.md) - How the app opens each cut cell into a flat pattern piece (slits along internal seams, automatic cuts for tubes), flattens it (cylinder unroll then ARAP with an envelope Cholesky solve), uses the result as cloth-space UVs and as the printable PDF pattern with ease and seam allowance.

* [Benchmark rehearsal and tool coverage (P8)](rehearsal-and-coverage.md) (draft) - The 13 moodboard benchmark designs rebuilt from their photos with only the designer app's commands (scripts in app/rehearsals, designs in app/designs), each compared side by side with its photo; per-design results, frame costs, rounds and remaining gaps; and an audit of the planned tool space (T1-T14, M1-M10) against what is built. # Technique

* [Drafted blocks](drafted-blocks.md) (draft) - The project's own leotard blocks, November 2026: drawn from a body's tape measures in true curves with seam joins decided in advance. 17 blocks (six app bodies, eleven adult sizes), all but XXS passing 42 pattern checks; six fitted on their own bodies. Calibrated, unreviewed, not yet in the app.
* [Fitting a block like the app](fitting-a-block-like-the-app.md) (draft) - November 2026: why drafted blocks fitted badly at the seat and thighs: leg cuts are now the purchased block's own, with named, tunable elastic and fabric that gathers; a line tuned to the app's look and a hard crotch pin were rejected and removed.
* [Fit solver realism audit](fit-solver-realism-audit.md) (draft) - November 2026: a sound geometric fit, not a realistic cloth simulation; fifteen ranked differences from public simulators and research, and the order of work before any speed-up.
* [Refitting after an edit](refitting-after-an-edit.md) (draft) - November 2026: first timing and accuracy of a re-fit after a cutout, started from the existing fit, on one body.
* [The flat and 3D link](flat-and-3d-link.md) (draft) - Stage 4 prototype, 2026-11-01: artwork lives on one canvas per cut piece, the garment wears those canvases and the PDF prints them. Round trip exact, seam crossings continuous, export true to scale. Dev-only at /wrap.html; not in the app, and unproven on real fabric.
* [The app's flat pattern against a real block](flat-pattern-against-a-real-block.md) - Measured on 2026-11-01: the young body is nearest block size XS. Total trunk length matches, but the app's flattened pieces follow body bumps, shift the shoulder seam, have a much shorter sleeve with a lower sleeve head, and one uniform ease that is too tight at the waist and too loose at bust and hip.
* [Wrapping a flat block onto the body](wrapping-a-flat-block-onto-the-body.md) (draft) - Stage 3 spike, 2026-11-01: a purchased block's flat pieces, seams welded, solved onto the garment surface in about four minutes for five solves. Under 0.1% inside out, zero seam gap, stretch close to the block's intended ease; a neckline cut can reuse the fit, a large leg cut should not. The map is host triangles the app's own renderer can use.
